items.toString:
RHEL4NV (el10nv) ships an inbox mlx5_core that does not support all SR-IOV test scenarios for CX-8/CX-9 NICs. Developed a new beakerlib pre-task (/kernel/networking/tools/ofed-install) to automate MLNX OFED 26.04 OOT driver setup before SR-IOV tests on RHEL4NV aarch64 Beaker jobs.

h3. Work Completed

* Implemented two-phase beakerlib task: phase 1 installs kernel-64k packages and reboots via rstrnt-reboot; phase 2 installs OFED RPMs after reboot on +64k kernel
* Applied --nodeps workaround for RHEL-184104 (kernel-core el10nv missing ksym() virtual provides blocking kmod RPM installation)
* Merged to kernel-qe/kernel master via MR 14420; dkms dependency fix open as MR 14422
* Filed RHEL-184797: dkms not available in official RHEL4NV repos (BaseOS/AppStream/CRB), only in EPEL — required for MLNX OFED kmod RPM installation
* Validated OOT driver on wsfd-advnetlab-amp04 (BOS2): mlx5_core loaded from updates/mlnx-ofa_kernel/, version 26.04-0.8.5, supported=external, mlx_compat loaded
* Root-caused SR-IOV test failure (lib_mlx.sh 'No MLNX_OFED package' + VF creation failure) to incomplete OFED base RPM install caused by missing dkms; resolved by MR 14422

h3. References

* MR 14420 (merged): [https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/kernel-qe/kernel/-/merge_requests/14420|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/kernel-qe/kernel/-/merge_requests/14420]
* MR 14422 (open - dkms fix): [https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/kernel-qe/kernel/-/merge_requests/14422|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/kernel-qe/kernel/-/merge_requests/14422]
* RHEL-184797: dkms missing from RHEL4NV official repos — [https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHEL-184797|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHEL-184797]
* RHEL-184104: kernel-core el10nv missing ksym() virtual provides — [https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHEL-184104|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHEL-184104]

items.fromString:
h2. Goal

Develop MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers for Beaker and Polarion, and integrate them with existing Jenkins and JIRA MCP servers to enable an AI-driven end-to-end automated testing workflow - from resource provisioning through test execution to result reporting.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] Beaker MCP server implemented with at least machine reserve/release capability
* [ ] Polarion MCP server implemented with at least Test Run creation and result update capability
* [ ] All four MCP servers (Beaker, Polarion, Jenkins, JIRA) connected to an AI agent (Gemini CLI or Claude Code)
* [ ] E2E workflow demonstrated: resource provisioning, test execution, result reporting, and status syncing via a single natural language prompt
* [ ] MCP server source code committed with README documentation

h2. Open Questions

* [ ] Who will own this Epic?
* [ ] Which repository will host the Beaker and Polarion MCP servers?
* [ ] Should the MCP servers be contributed upstream or maintained internally?

h2. External Resources

* [MCP Official Docs|https://modelcontextprotocol.io/] - Model Context Protocol specification
* [Beaker API Documentation|https://beaker-project.org/docs/server-api/index.html]
* [Pylero (Polarion Python SDK)|https://pypi.org/project/pylero/]

items.fromString:
Ethernet-focused companion to [NHE-2288|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/NHE-2288], which covers the InfiniBand path. This ticket documents the Ethernet/RoCE/Spectrum-X multi-plane networking components on RHEL for NVIDIA 26.01 (kernel 6.12 baseline) and provides three Ethernet-focused architecture maps.

h2. Why Ethernet?

Ethernet (RoCE / Spectrum-X) is now the dominant deployment model for new hyperscale AI clusters. As of 2025, Ethernet holds ~60-70% of the AI back-end network market (Dell'Oro Group) -- more than double the size of InfiniBand. Meta Llama 3, OpenAI Stargate, Oracle, and SoftBank all deploy on RoCE / Spectrum-X. NVIDIA's own GB200 NVL72 platform is transitioning from NVLink8+IB to NVLink72+Spectrum-X.

See attached {{ib-vs-ethernet-market-analysis.md}} for full market data and sources.

h2. Key Differences: Ethernet Path vs. InfiniBand Path

|| Aspect || InfiniBand (NHE-2288) || Ethernet (This ticket) ||
| Switch hardware | Quantum-3 NDR/XDR | Spectrum-4 (Spectrum-X) |
| Fabric management | UFM v6.4+ (IB SM + AR + SHIELD) | SONiC / Cumulus Linux (PFC/ECN/ECMP) |
| Congestion control | ooo_sl_mask / IB adaptive routing | PFC + ECN + DCQCN |
| Packet spraying | IB AR at switch | Spectrum-X per-packet ECMP |
| UFM required | Yes | No |
| Open standard | NVIDIA-proprietary IB AR | UEC 1.0 (June 2025) |
| NCCL mechanism | 0-byte RDMA_WRITE_WITH_IMM trick | Standard RoCE (spray at switch) |
| UCX setting | UCX_IB_AR_ENABLE | UCX_NET_DEVICES per GID |
| IB sub-devices | SMI per plane / NEWDEV/DELDEV | Not needed |

h2. Component Status on RHEL 10 / RHEL for NVIDIA (Ethernet Path)

|| Component || Status in RHEL 10 (6.12) || Action Required ||
| mlx5e 8-port LAG | Already in 6.12 | None |
| mlx5e 4-port E-switch | Already in 6.12 | None |
| mlx5e RoCE base support | Already in 6.12 | None |
| mlx5e 800G Ethernet | Not in 6.12 (6.13 feature) | Backport from 6.13 or DOCA-OFED |
| DCQCN congestion control | Partial in 6.12 | Configure via mlx5 debugfs |
| NetworkManager / iproute2 | Ships in RHEL 10 | Reconfigure: PFC, ECN, DSCP trust |
| rdma-core / libibverbs | Ships in RHEL 10 | Minor update for RoCE GID management |
| UCX | Ships in RHEL 10 | Update: GID-based multi-rail, UCX_NET_DEVICES |
| MPI libraries | Ships in RHEL 10 | Disable eager-rdma and RDMA-Fast-Path |
| NCCL | Not in RHEL | New install required (NVIDIA provides v2.12+) |
| SONiC / Cumulus Linux | Not in RHEL | New install: switch NOS for Spectrum-4 |
| DOCA-OFED | Not in RHEL | New install via DKMS (GPUDirect + 800G) |
| GPUDirect RDMA over RoCE | DMA-BUF in 6.12, uncertified | DOCA-OFED for production |
| UEC 1.0 stack | Not in RHEL | Emerging standard, evolving 2025+ |
| OpenSM | Ships in RHEL 10 | Not needed for Ethernet path |
| UFM | Not in RHEL | Not needed for Ethernet path |

h2. Architecture Maps (attached)

Three Mermaid architecture maps covering the Ethernet multi-plane path:

* {{map-eth1-nvidia-ethernet-stack.png}} -- Map E1: Pure NVIDIA Ethernet multi-plane stack (7 layers, SONiC/CoSci/UEC instead of UFM/IB-AR)
* {{map-eth2-rhel10-ethernet.png}} -- Map E2: RHEL 10 (kernel 6.12) Ethernet components, color-coded by action needed, Ethernet path only
* {{map-eth3-rhel4nv-ethernet.png}} -- Map E3: RHEL for NVIDIA 26.01 Ethernet path, includes GB200/NVLink/GPU passthrough layer

Mermaid source for all three maps is in the attached {{multiplane-component-maps-ethernet.md}}.

items.fromString:
This task tracks the Ethernet-focused QE test plan for validating NVIDIA multi-plane Ethernet network topology features on RHEL for NVIDIA 26.01 (kernel 6.12 baseline). This is a companion to the IB-focused plan [NHE-2297|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/NHE-2297].

The full test plan is attached as {{multiplane-ethernet-qe-test-plan.md}}.

h2. Why Ethernet?

Ethernet (RoCE / Spectrum-X) is now the dominant deployment model for new hyperscale AI clusters — Meta Llama 3, OpenAI Stargate, Oracle, and SoftBank are all on RoCE/Spectrum-X as of 2025. Ethernet has overtaken InfiniBand with ~60-70% of the AI back-end network market (Dell'Oro Group, 2025). NVIDIA's own GB200 NVL72 platform is transitioning from NVLink8+IB to NVLink72+Spectrum-X.

h2. Key Differences from IB Multi-Plane Plan

* No SMI sub-devices or UFM — switch management via SONiC/Cumulus
* Congestion control is PFC/ECN/DSCP (not adaptive routing via ooo_sl_mask)
* Packet spraying is Spectrum-X per-packet ECMP at switch level (not IB adaptive routing)
* Switch hardware: Spectrum-4 (not Quantum-3)
* No UFM license required

h2. Scope

Ethernet multi-plane specific features under test:

|| Area || Source / Kernel ||
| CX-9 dual-mode: Ethernet / RoCE configuration | DOCA-OFED |
| PFC (Priority Flow Control) lossless configuration | mlx5e / NetworkManager |
| ECN (Explicit Congestion Notification) | mlx5e / kernel |
| DSCP trust and traffic class mapping | mlx5e |
| RoCE GID selection for multi-plane | rdma-core |
| Spectrum-X per-packet ECMP (packet spraying) | Spectrum-4 switch firmware |
| SONiC / Cumulus switch configuration for AI fabric | SONiC / Cumulus |
| NVIDIA Spectrum-X CoSci congestion control | Spectrum-4 firmware |
| mlx5e 8-port LAG | kernel 6.12 (in RHEL4NV) |
| mlx5e 4-port E-switch / multiport SR-IOV + RoCE offload | kernel 6.12 (in RHEL4NV) |
| UCX multi-rail over RoCE (one rail per Ethernet plane) | UCX >= 1.12.0 |
| NCCL over RoCE with packet spraying | NCCL >= 2.12 |
| GPUDirect RDMA over RoCE (GPU HBM to NIC DMA) | DOCA-OFED required |
| Ethernet multi-plane failover and recovery | all of the above |
| 800G Ethernet link speed on CX-9 | 6.13 backport / DOCA-OFED |

h2. Hardware (ARM-First Priority)

*Option A (ARM-First):* 2x ARM server + 2x CX-9 dual-port + 2x Spectrum-4 switches (SONiC/Cumulus)
*Option B (Grace Blackwell):* 2x GB200 NVL + 2x Spectrum-4 switches

No UFM license needed for the Ethernet path.

h2. Test Cases (14 total, TC-ETH-001 through TC-ETH-014)

|| ID || Title || Priority ||
| TC-ETH-001 | CX-9 Ethernet/RoCE Mode Configuration | P0 |
| TC-ETH-002 | PFC Lossless Configuration | P0 |
| TC-ETH-003 | ECN Congestion Notification | P1 |
| TC-ETH-004 | DSCP Trust and Traffic Class Mapping | P1 |
| TC-ETH-005 | Per-Packet ECMP / Spectrum-X Packet Spraying | P0 |
| TC-ETH-006 | Spectrum-X CoSci Congestion Control | P1 |
| TC-ETH-007 | 8-Port Ethernet LAG | P1 |
| TC-ETH-008 | 4-Port Ethernet E-switch (Multiport SR-IOV + RoCE) | P1 |
| TC-ETH-009 | UCX Multi-Rail over RoCE | P0 |
| TC-ETH-010 | NCCL AllReduce over RoCE Multi-Plane | P1 |
| TC-ETH-011 | GPUDirect RDMA over RoCE | P1 |
| TC-ETH-012 | 800G Ethernet Link Speed on CX-9 | P1 |
| TC-ETH-013 | Ethernet Multi-Plane Failover and Recovery | P1 |
| TC-ETH-014 | SONiC Switch Configuration for AI Fabric | P1 |

Each test case includes objective, prerequisites, step-by-step procedure, expected result, and ASCII traffic diagram.

h2. Related

* IB-focused test plan: [NHE-2297|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/NHE-2297]
* Research ticket: [NHE-2288|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/NHE-2288]

items.toString:
Ethernet-focused QE test plan for validating NVIDIA multi-plane Ethernet (RoCE/Spectrum-X) network topology features on RHEL for NVIDIA 26.01 (kernel 6.12 baseline).

Ethernet multi-plane is now the dominant deployment model for new hyperscale AI clusters (Meta, OpenAI Stargate, Oracle, SoftBank). This plan focuses on the RoCE / Spectrum-X path and is a parallel document to the IB plan in NHE-2297.

h2. Sister Tickets

|| Ticket || Type || Focus ||
| [NHE-2288|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/NHE-2288] | Research | IB software components research + architecture maps |
| [NHE-2297|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/NHE-2297] | Task | IB QE test plan — parallel to this ticket |
| [NHE-2299|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/NHE-2299] | Research | Ethernet component maps + market analysis |

h2. Deliverables

* *ethernet-qe-test-plan.md* — Ethernet multi-plane QE test plan: hardware topology, minimum HW BOM, 14 test cases (TC-ETH-001 through TC-ETH-014) with ASCII traffic diagrams

h2. Scope

14 test cases covering:
* TC-ETH-001: CX-9 Ethernet/RoCE mode configuration
* TC-ETH-002: PFC (Priority Flow Control) lossless configuration
* TC-ETH-003: ECN (Explicit Congestion Notification) and DCQCN
* TC-ETH-004: DSCP trust and traffic class mapping
* TC-ETH-005: Per-packet ECMP across Ethernet planes (Spectrum-X packet spraying)
* TC-ETH-006: Spectrum-X CoSci congestion control
* TC-ETH-007: 8-port Ethernet LAG (kernel 6.12)
* TC-ETH-008: 4-port Ethernet E-switch / multiport SR-IOV
* TC-ETH-009: UCX multi-rail over RoCE
* TC-ETH-010: NCCL AllReduce over RoCE multi-plane
* TC-ETH-011: GPUDirect RDMA over RoCE
* TC-ETH-012: 800G Ethernet link speed
* TC-ETH-013: Ethernet multi-plane failover and recovery
* TC-ETH-014: SONiC switch configuration for AI fabric

h2. Hardware Topology

ARM-first (HIGHER PRIORITY): ARM servers with CX-9 dual-port PCIe NICs in Ethernet/RoCE mode + Spectrum-4 switches.
Minimum: 2 compute nodes, 2 CX-9 dual-port NICs, 2 Spectrum-4 switches (one per plane, SONiC/Cumulus), 1 management server.
No UFM needed — switch managed via standard Ethernet tools (SONiC CLI / Cumulus NCLU).

h2. Key Prerequisites

* OS: RHEL for NVIDIA 26.01 (kernel 6.12.x, aarch64)
* DOCA-Host 3.x (DOCA-OFED DKMS) — required for RoCE + GPUDirect RDMA
* SONiC or Cumulus Linux on Spectrum-4 switches
* UCX >= 1.12.0 (built with RoCE/ibverbs support), NCCL >= 2.12
* mlnx_qos tool (PFC configuration), perftest package

| mlx5_ib SMI sub-device per plane (NEWDEV/DELDEV) | 6.12 (in RHEL4NV) |
